error: missing required argument 'target'

Usage: mcp-surface [options] <target...>

Smoke-test an MCP server: connect, read its tool surface, validate it, and diff
against a recorded snapshot.

Arguments:
  target                       URL of a remote server, or the command and
                               arguments that start a local one

Options:
  --transport <kind>           force transport: stdio | http | sse (default:
                               inferred)
  --cwd <dir>                  working directory for a stdio server
  -e, --env <KEY=VALUE>        environment variable for a stdio server
                               (repeatable)
  -H, --header <KEY=VALUE>     HTTP header for a remote server (repeatable)
  --timeout <ms>               per-request timeout in milliseconds (default:
                               20000)
  --snapshot <file>            compare the surface against this snapshot file
  --update-snapshot            write the current surface to the snapshot file
                               instead of comparing
  --skip <rule>                rule or check id to ignore (repeatable)
  --max-tools <n>              warn above this many tools (default: 40)
  --max-definition-bytes <n>   warn when serialised tool definitions exceed this
                               many bytes (default: 16384)
  --max-description-chars <n>  note descriptions longer than this (default:
                               1024)
  --fail-on <level>            exit non-zero at this level or above: error |
                               warn | info (default: "error")
  --call                       additionally invoke each tool that declares
                               readOnlyHint and takes no required arguments, and
                               report the result
  --json                       emit machine-readable JSON instead of the text
                               report
  --json-out <file>            also write the JSON report here, keeping the text
                               report on stdout
  -V, --version                output the version number
  -h, --help                   display help for command
